clue.text: Picture of girl kept by her parents

indicators.note: something kept by another is held within it, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a girl's parents are her PA and MA
Nora is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A daughter's photograph is treasured by her mother and father.
explanation.definitionFit: A panorama is a wide, sweeping view or picture of a scene.

clue.text: Exist without party, love?

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so one word wraps round the other

parts.note: to exist is to be, as in 'they are'
a do is a party or celebration

explanation.surface: A wistful question about whether love can survive without celebrations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, not lacking, which the comma-led surface hides.
explanation.definitionFit: To adore someone is to love them deeply; the question mark flags the verb sense.

clue.text: Paid in cash coming from Pip's friend

parts.note: something coming from a place is out of it
Herbert Pocket is Pip's friend in Dickens's Great Expectations

explanation.surface: Someone receives cash payment from a friend called Pip.
explanation.walkthrough: Pip is the hero of Dickens's Great Expectations, and Herbert Pocket is his close friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Out-of-pocket expenses are those a person has paid personally, typically in cash.

clue.text: Mice NASA put in orbit may be showing brain disorder

indicators.note: sending something into orbit spins it round, so these letters are tumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: Mice launched into space by NASA might come back with neurological problems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put in orbit' rearranges MICE and NASA.
explanation.definitionFit: An amnesiac person suffers memory loss, a disorder of the brain.

clue.text: Kept building in Britain as decreed by government

definitions.text: Kept building in Britain as decreed by government

parts.words: Kept building in Britain as decreed by government
parts.note: reads like an ongoing construction project, but 'kept' means preserved: an old structure the state has ordered protected

explanation.surface: The government has ordered building work in Britain to continue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kept building' looks like 'went on building', but it is a structure that is kept, i.e. legally preserved.
explanation.definitionFit: A scheduled ancient monument in Britain is an old structure protected by government order.

clue.text: Florid style of cardigan initially introduced by jumper company

indicators.note: a letter introduced by a word is slipped inside it

parts.note: a roo, short for kangaroo, is a jumper

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of cardigan

explanation.surface: A fussy cardigan design launched by a knitwear firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumper' suggests knitwear beside 'cardigan', but it is a kangaroo, ROO, which takes in C.
explanation.definitionFit: Rococo is an elaborately ornamented eighteenth-century decorative style.

clue.text: Republican or Democrat's last statement

indicators.note: last picks the final letter of Democrat

explanation.surface: A political statement from either party in American politics.
explanation.definitionFit: A report is an account or formal statement of facts.

clue.text: Not entirely attractive drunk

indicators.note: not entirely means the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: cute means attractive or pretty

explanation.surface: Someone drunk is not entirely as attractive as they think.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not entirely' drops the last letter of CUTE.
explanation.definitionFit: Cut is informal slang for drunk, as in half-cut.

clue.text: Anxious about old pound note turning up where criminals meet

parts.note: C, for circa, means about
a oncer was old slang for a one-pound note

indicators.note: in a down answer, turning up means the word is written bottom to top

parts.note: a den is a hideout where criminals gather

explanation.surface: Someone worries about an old banknote turning up in a thieves' hangout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' reverses DEN to NED. A ONCER was the British one-pound note, withdrawn in the 1980s.
explanation.definitionFit: Being concerned is being worried or anxious about something.

clue.text: Temper succeeded in many instances

parts.note: S is a standard abbreviation for succeeded in genealogies
often means on many occasions

explanation.surface: A bad temper usually wins through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Temper' looks like a noun for anger, but it is the verb: to moderate.
explanation.definitionFit: To temper something is to moderate or soften it.

clue.text: Part of coping with opencast working

indicators.note: working suggests the letters being worked over into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Dealing with the strain of an open-cast mine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coping' looks like managing stress, but it is the top course of a wall.
explanation.definitionFit: A capstone is one of the stones forming the protective top course of a wall, its coping.

clue.text: Subservient labourer needing some self-respect to return

indicators.note: to return means the picked letters are read backwards
some means only a part of the words is used

explanation.surface: A lowly worker who needs to regain some self-esteem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' takes FRES from inside self-respect, and 'to return' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A serf was a feudal labourer bound to work his lord's land.

clue.text: Where a tar's shot seabird

indicators.note: shot means wrecked or ruined, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Asking where a sailor shot a seabird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' rearranges WHERE A TARS; the 's is part of the fodder here.
explanation.definitionFit: A shearwater is an ocean seabird that skims low over the waves.

clue.text: Navy office had similar upset over introduction of pinnace

indicators.note: in a down answer, over places the first part above the next
upset means knocked over, so the letters are disturbed into a new order
introduction of points to the opening letter of pinnace

explanation.surface: A naval office had a similar upset involving a small ship's boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges HAD SIMILAR, which sits 'over' the P that opens pinnace.
explanation.definitionFit: An admiralship is the office or rank of an admiral in a navy.

clue.text: Ill-mannered number I allow to go outside

indicators.note: one word going outside another wraps round it

parts.note: to grant is to allow

explanation.surface: A rude number one refuses to allow outdoors.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pairs 'number' with 'I' as one phrase, but the I stands first in the answer and only the number sits inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Ignorant is used informally for rude or discourteous, lacking manners.

clue.text: Sycophant getting president Cleveland to introduce measure once

indicators.note: to introduce one thing into another sets it within

parts.note: Grover Cleveland was a US president
the ell was an old measure of length

explanation.surface: A flatterer gets a US president to bring in an old unit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to introduce' puts ELL into GROVER.
explanation.definitionFit: A groveller fawns on others in a servile way, like a sycophant.

clue.text: A large number of human beings yearn not to make money

parts.note: man means humankind, human beings collectively

indicators.note: not means the following piece is excluded from the word

parts.note: to earn is to make money

explanation.surface: Many people long for something other than getting rich.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes EARN from YEARN, leaving Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Many, as in 'many people', means a large number of.

clue.text: Tower guard loses fine bird

indicators.note: loses means a letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: a Beefeater is a Yeoman Warder at the Tower of London
F is the pencil-grading abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: A Tower guard is fined and loses his bird.
explanation.walkthrough: Beefeaters are the ceremonial guards at the Tower of London; it famously keeps ravens, which feeds the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: The bee-eater is a brightly coloured bird that catches bees in flight.

clue.text: Soldiers go in here when Grand Old Duke changes direction

indicators.note: changes direction swaps R for right into L for left

parts.note: the nursery rhyme's Grand Old Duke of York

explanation.surface: Troops march in where the Grand Old Duke turns them about.
explanation.walkthrough: The rhyme has the Duke march his men up and down a hill. Soldiers are also British toast strips, dipped into a boiled egg.
explanation.definitionFit: Soldiers, strips of buttered toast, are dipped into the runny part of a boiled egg.

clue.text: Annul order I've sent out

indicators.note: sent out suggests the letters dispatched and scattered into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Cancel the instructions I have issued.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent out' rearranges ORDER and IVE.
explanation.definitionFit: To override a decision is to set it aside or annul it.

clue.text: Empty interior used in conjuror's illusion

indicators.note: used in means placed inside the other word

parts.note: a mage is a magician or conjuror

indicators.note: empty means the inside letters are removed, leaving the first and last

explanation.surface: A conjuror's trick uses a hollow inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Empty' leaves IR from interior, and 'used in' puts it in MAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A mirage is an optical illusion, such as water seen in a desert.

clue.text: As spinner, one wants suffocating atmosphere in the middle

indicators.note: in places the pair inside the word for the middle

parts.note: the centre is the middle
I is the Roman numeral one
a fug is a stuffy, airless atmosphere

explanation.surface: A cricket spinner wants a stifling atmosphere in midfield.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spinner' suggests a cricket bowler, but it is a laboratory machine; 'As' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A centrifuge is a machine that spins samples rapidly to separate them.

clue.text: Rounded part in model of Earth's no good

indicators.note: no means the next piece is left out

parts.note: a globe is a model of the Earth; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: A globe is useless in showing part of the world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no' removes G from GLOBE.
explanation.definitionFit: A lobe is a rounded projecting part, as of the ear or a leaf.

clue.text: Material clothing sailor's run up

indicators.note: in a down answer, run up means the pieces are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: kit means clothing or gear
AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor

explanation.surface: Fabric for clothing a sailor has sewn together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'run up' looks like sewing, but it reverses KIT and AB together.
explanation.definitionFit: Batik is a fabric decorated with wax-resist dyeing.

clue.text: Dull herbal tea I may share with someone

parts.note: flat means dull or lifeless
maté is a South American herbal tea

explanation.surface: Offering a dreary herbal tea to share with a guest.
explanation.definitionFit: A flatmate is someone with whom a home is shared, here speaking as 'I'.

clue.text: Can of dye remaining unfinished

indicators.note: a word left unfinished loses its final letter

parts.note: a tint is a dye or colouring

explanation.surface: A tin of dye that is still not used up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'remaining unfinished' drops the last letter of TINT.
explanation.definitionFit: A tin is a metal can for food or paint.

clue.text: One that's taken turn round island — this one?

definitions.text: One that's taken turn round island — this one?

indicators.note: round means wrapped around the island letter
letters that have taken a turn are twisted into a new order

parts.note: the word that, with its 's as is
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A traveller circling an island wonders whether this is the one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken turn' rearranges THAT to TAHT; 'round' puts it about I for island, and One adds I. The whole clue then hints at an island.
explanation.definitionFit: Tahiti is a Pacific island in French Polynesia.

clue.text: Tree that's old, having spread

parts.note: a range is a spread, as of prices or options

explanation.surface: An ancient tree with widespread branches.
explanation.definitionFit: An orange is a citrus tree as well as its fruit.

clue.text: Twist mediaeval weapon — it takes its toll

parts.note: to turn is to twist
a pike is a long mediaeval spear

explanation.surface: A medieval weapon given a twist takes a heavy toll.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes its toll' sounds like causing harm, but a turnpike is a road with tolls.
explanation.definitionFit: A turnpike is a road or gate where travellers pay a toll.
